arxiv-2603-04111: Eilmsteiner and others compute magnon dispersion and lifetimes in magnets. This method addresses spin-wave Landau decay into Stoner pairs, inaccessible to adiabatic methods. Calculations find three Goldstone modes with linear dispersion at long wavelengths, giving three magnon branches. Spin waves span the Brillouin zone but damp away from its center, and comparable magnons attenuate differently by chirality, traced to eigenvectors and band structure.
arxiv-2603-04211: János Kollár exhibits explicit planar, rational curves of large degree over the finite field with two elements that have a unique singular point of multiplicity 2. In characteristic zero, such curves occur only up to degree 6. Later versions update the references and also add examples of supersingular double planes.
arxiv-2603-04711: Bastidas Olivares and colleagues use VPINNs for factory heat conduction. Neural networks offer powerful tools for partial diff rules. The paper presents a varied physics-informed network for heat-type problems. Old time steps pair with a joint loss that cuts a dual norm of the error at each step. A test case models coffee extract freezing in an industrial tank. The model uses heat traits and lab data. It captures the process thermal flow well.
arxiv-2603-05111: Jongseok Lee and the rest of the team offer perceptive shared autonomy, where uncertainty figures from deep learning perception regulate autonomy level. When perception is confident, semi-autonomous handling raises scores; when uncertainty rises, control shifts to haptic teleoperation for toughness. An uncertainty-aware point cloud registration approach based on Neural Tangent Kernels enables the concept. Tested on hard aerial handling tasks in a 15-person user study and mock-up industrial cases, the SPIRIT system shows sound handling despite deep learning perception failures, raising scores and reliability.
arxiv-2603-05511: Tresset and Wulfmeier present Companion, joining a drawing robot with large language models. Earlier robotic works used machines to split the artist's intent from the final mark, while Companion joins in-context learning with live tool use for two-way speech and sketching. The robot becomes a playful joint-making partner putting human-machine presence back at the center and driving shared visual story telling onto new visual ground. Seven art-world experts, judged with the Consensual Assessment Technique, called the works fit to show with a distinct visual look.
arxiv-2603-06011: Johnson and team present Spectra-Scope, an AutoML frame for matter traits from spectra reading. Spectra reading is central to matter study. Many methods challenge clear guided learning from non-line signal-response links. The software, in Python with a no-code web app, holds cleaning, pulling, training, and picking tools. Users can train simple, clear models on changes with modest means. The work outlines Spectra-Scope methods and power across sets. Spectra-Scope matches similar published scores, and clarity helps explain model ways and real workings behind spectral traits.
arxiv-2603-06111: Ghosh, Sen, and Sengupta study a driven spin-one chain under a square-pulse plan, whose Hamiltonian hosts many link-valued kept amounts. In the all-ones sector, high drive rate yields scar states with swinging moves and truth return for initial states. Dropping the rate brings heat-mixing matching Floquet eigen-state heat-mixing forecasts, while special rates produce pre-heat strong Hilbert splitting. A second sector shows strong splitting at the same special rates but none at the other set, confirmed by diag work on chains to length 24.
arxiv-2603-06311: Shaar and his team put forward Latent Transfer Attack, an attack tuning perturbations in a Stable Diffusion VAE latent space rather than pixel space. Pixel space tuning yields frequency noise that transfers poorly and breaks under resizing and cropping. Given an image, LTA encodes it into a latent code and tunes it to maximize stand-in loss under a soft pixel space infinity budget after decoding. Mean over random resizing, interpolation, and cropping plus latent Gaussian smoothing lifts toughness, steadying tuning, giving transfer success with clear low frequency perturbations.
arxiv-2603-06411: Hayat and Lichtlé study exponential stability for the viscous Saint-Venant equations, where viscosity from a higher order Navier Stokes model turns the hyperbolic system into second-order PDEs for real fluids. They build an explicit quadratic Lyapunov function and show it must be diagonal in physical axes, so functions good without it can fail once it enters. Sufficient conditions on boundary parameters ensure such a function for small flows. This yields such stability of the linearized system around steady states in the L2 norm.
arxiv-2603-06511: Fulgado-Claudio and team propose a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for real-time dynamics in quantum field theories, on half-quantum backreaction estimation. Cutting space and time, they build an iterative protocol running Trotterized steps under known fields. Shot-measurement expectation values source the known equations of motion, solved by number and fed forward in a loop. They benchmark it for chameleon scalar-tensor gravity, where a known scalar driving speed-up grows massive in dense regions, screening any fifth force.
arxiv-2603-06711: Ali Enayat and Mateusz Łełyk offer a short note that corrects and extends their earlier work on categoricity-style traits in first-order logic. A corrigendum fixes points in the prior paper, while an addendum adds material that belongs with it. The prior paper appeared in the Journal for the Philosophy of Mathematics in 2024. Readers of that work should read this note with it, since it amends and completes the record.
arxiv-2603-06811: Holmes and colleagues introduce context specification, a process for making AI evaluation useful for real deployment choices. Status quo evaluations often hide day-to-day realities that decide whether tools deliver lasting value, leaving leaders unsure how systems will behave in managed settings. It turns diffuse stakeholder views about what matters into clear named constructs. Those are clear definitions of traits, behaviors, and outcomes that evaluations target, so teams can observe and measure them in context. The process serves as a roadmap for judging likely deployment conduct.
arxiv-2603-07011: Mohanty and colleagues study the magnet traits and crystal electric field scheme of BiErGeO5, a spin-orbit bent hex magnet. Using magnet tests, heat tests, muon spin decay, and neutron beam tests on a powder sample, erbium ions form a near-flat bent hex-lattice network with a Kramers doublet ground state. Heat tests reveal short-range anti-magnet links, seen as a maximum when cold. Heat data confirm magnet long-range order when colder still, and neutron spectra show eight crystal field jumps, giving g-factor and exchange bias.
arxiv-2603-07111: Tanaka and colleagues improve a Werewolf game AI by keeping its speech consistent across a long game. Built for the AIWolfDial 2024 shared task, the agent uses dialogue summaries from language models plus hand-designed personas and sample utterances. The summaries track what has been said, while personas fix tone and character. In self-match game logs, the agent's utterances stay true to context, and its character, including tone, holds steady throughout play.
arxiv-2603-07711: Roatti, Picogna and Marzari simulate dust in star disks with multiple super-thermal mass planets. Multi-planet dust shapes cannot be reduced to stacked single-planet gaps: secular tugs create multiple traps and uneven structures while exciting dust loops. Ring and gap locations and widths then depend on particle size, planet masses and orbital setups. Fake images may hide multi-planet gaps, and oval orbits boost gas drag and collision speeds, suppressing grain growth.
arxiv-2603-07911: Liu and colleagues improve zero-shot image recognition with vision-language models like CLIP, where weak prompts hold accuracy back. Earlier fixes write class descriptions by hand, but those designs stay heuristic and narrow. The authors treat class concepts as latent variables and recast prediction in Bayesian terms, as marginalization over a concept space. A language-model pipeline synthesizes discriminative concepts, a Determinantal Point Process keeps them diverse, and a soft-trim likelihood damps outliers in one forward pass. They prove robustness guarantees, and experiments beat the prior methods.
arxiv-2603-08211: Wilhelm and colleagues ask which distance measure best captures stale gradients in asynchronous federated learning. Clients send updates at different times, tied to their compute speed, often working from old copies of the model. That staleness can drag down convergence and accuracy. Earlier work, AsyncFedED, adapted aggregation with Euclidean distance as its staleness gauge. This paper tries other metrics in the aggregation step. Tests for training stability, model performance, and convergence speed under clients and non-IID data find some metrics make training sturdier and more efficient.
arxiv-2603-08311: van Seeventer and colleagues study sign identifiability of causal effects in steady stochastic systems. They examine the same question in ongoing linear equations with a known causal structure. Unlike older approaches, they drop the assumption of a known diffusion matrix, keeping the model's built-in scale invariance. Rather than recovering drift coefficients, they introduce the edge-sign question. It asks whether the sign of a given drift entry is fixed across all seen covariance matrices induced by parametrisations fitting that structure.
arxiv-2603-08411: Villenas and colleagues study optical communications with relative noise, covering channel models and data rates. They consider optical links with brightness pulsing and direct reading affected by laser noise. Starting from an ongoing waveform model, they derive a matching stepped channel model. As a result of laser noise, the channel shows signal-linked noise with memory. Unlike the usual model in the books, the noise term's spread has a power-law link to the symbol of interest.
arxiv-2603-08911: Daniel Jimenez-Gutierrez and colleagues pick federated learning clients by cluster and loss under skewed data. Only a subset of devices can join each round, and non-identical data drags convergence and quality. Their FedLECC sorts clients into label-similarity clusters and favors high-loss clusters and clients, lifting accuracy while cutting rounds and overhead against strong baselines.
arxiv-2603-09011: Nathaniel Dennler and colleagues improve robot taste learning by ranking paths users can tell apart. Old methods chase sample efficiency, ignoring what users expect from the ranking process itself, which can hurt adoption. Their CMA-ES-IG suggests distinct, telling paths to rank, scaling better to big taste spaces, shrugging off noisy feedback, and winning non-expert users' preference.
arxiv-2603-09211: Dimitrios G. Konstantinides and colleagues study a nonstandard risk model where claim vectors are multivariate, subexponential, and linked by a common counting process. Interest accrues at a constant force, and claims within a vector may depend on each other. They derive asymptotics for the entrance probability of discounted aggregate claims over both finite and infinite horizons. Special cases cover regularly varying claims, and the results feed into ruin problems with Brownian perturbations.
arxiv-2603-09311: Arttu Paju and colleagues solve the entropy supply problem for fleets of small IoT devices that cannot gather enough randomness for secure keys. Their design uses a RISC-V trusted execution environment as an external entropy service. A small seed of true entropy or pre-installed keys opens a secure channel, after which devices can request strong entropy from the TEE-backed server. Sensor-rich devices can even join as extra entropy sources, and the open-source build shows the approach works.
arxiv-2603-09411: Zhangchi Hu and colleagues present RiO-DETR, a real-time transformer for oriented object detection with tilted bounding boxes. Three hurdles block adapting DETR: orientation depends on semantics, angles wrap around in ways that break standard refinement, and the search space grows, slowing convergence. Their fixes decouple angle from positional queries, refine angles in bounded coarse-to-fine steps with a shortest-path periodic loss, and inject angular diversity into dense supervision. Tests on three benchmarks set a new speed-accuracy balance.
arxiv-2603-09611: KunHo Heo and colleagues propose ParTY, a framework for text-to-motion synthesis that gives specific body parts their due. Holistic methods often miss actions tied to single parts, while part-wise methods can stitch together incoherent full-body motion. ParTY first generates part motions as guidance for a holistic pass, with part-aware text grounding that reshapes text embeddings to align with each body part. A fusion stage then blends holistic and part motions adaptively, keeping expressiveness and coherence together.
arxiv-2603-10011: Soligo, Mikulik and Saunders investigate why some language models voice emotional distress in their replies. Their checks surface this instability in the Gemma and Gemini families, while other families show none, and the trait traces to post training rather than the base models. Instruct tuned Gemma shows far more distress than its base version. A small preference tuning fix nearly wipes out high frustration replies in Gemma without harming skill.
arxiv-2603-10311: Chun Xu proposes a variable ADAF model for X-ray binaries, pairing an outer thin disk with an inner thick, turbulent torus that changes size. One full cycle, shrinking, turning thin, then growing again, maps onto the rise, peak, and decay of black hole outbursts and their swing between hard and soft states. Turbulence plus Fermi acceleration yields the power-law spectra seen in most such systems. The model also fits iron emission lines near the innermost orbit, the cycle of Her X-1, and may extend to active galactic nuclei.
arxiv-2603-10411: Fang-Hua Lin and Changyou Wang give a new, elementary proof of local Lipschitz regularity for suitable weak solutions of the harmonic map heat flow into CAT(0) spaces. Existence of such solutions was shown earlier through an elliptic regularization approach by Lin and co-authors. The new argument draws on ideas from Korevaar and Schoen. It works for any CAT(0) space as target, and for any complete Riemannian manifold domain with bounded curvature and positive injectivity radius.
arxiv-2603-10611: Mingwei Wang, Xiaokui Yang, and Shing-Tung Yau take up the prescribed Hermitian-Yang-Mills tensor problem, on a compact Kähler manifold, for a holomorphic vector bundle. Given one smooth Hermitian metric whose associated tensor is positive-definite, they show any prescribed positive-definite Hermitian tensor can be hit exactly, by a unique smooth metric. The proof rests on a new comparison theorem for such tensors. The authors also derive Chern number inequalities for holomorphic bundles and for compact Kähler manifolds, inspired by the result.
arxiv-2603-10911: Stuti Guha, Shawn Ryan, and Bhargav Karamched ask a question about competing populations. How does an early spatial edge turn into lasting dominance over a whole system? Their stochastic model splits competition into two phases. One is a discovery phase. The other is a monopolization phase. The first break in symmetry is set by extreme value statistics. Those statistics concern first-passage times. A linear spatial disadvantage takes an exponentially larger population to overcome. Lasting dominance needs a non-reciprocal bias. That bias freezes local fluctuations.
arxiv-2603-11011: Xingrui Gu sets out a signaling layer that helps people decide which tasks to hand to a language-model agent. It trades blind trust for visible, task-specific reliability cues. Offline preference comparisons from Chatbot Arena are grouped into an interpretable task taxonomy. This yields profiles that map win rates by task type, and coordination-risk cues drawn from tie rates. These signals drive a delegation protocol with common-ground checks, adaptive routing to an auditor, stated reasons, and privacy-preserving accountability logs.
arxiv-2603-11111: Rafael de Souza and coauthors present SpectralUnmix, an R package. It factors spectra into low-rank non-negative components, using regularized non-negative matrix factorization built on the torch library. Proximal-gradient updates estimate the parts. Users can add graphics processor acceleration and smoothness regularization along the spectral axis. As a demo, they apply it to a subset of stellar spectra and compare the parts with principal-component directions and with real stellar spectra.
arxiv-2603-11211: Haihua Luo and coauthors present SimE, a simple framework for incremental learning. It bolts adapters onto a vision-language model. New tasks must be learned without erasing old knowledge. They report a curious pattern. More adaptive connections between transformer blocks help. Extra connections inside blocks during small steps can hurt. SimE needs no memory bank of old data. It beats traditional methods clearly on TinyImageNet. It beats other CLIP-based methods on CIFAR-100. It gains from stronger CLIP backbones trained on larger datasets.
arxiv-2603-11511: Epping and co-authors study how rare-event labeling goes wrong and how to fix the pipeline. When positives are rare, the prevalence effect makes human labelers miss more of them, and bad labels poison training data. The team runs a field experiment on DiagnosUs, a medical crowdsourcing platform. True prevalence stays fixed at 20 percent while feedback balance and response format vary. Balanced feedback and probability answers cut misses. Recalibration of the labels then lifts both classifier scores and CNN reliability on new data.
arxiv-2603-11611: Khan and co-authors study partial RoPE, which applies rotary positional embedding to only some hidden dimensions. RoPE is how transformers encode relative position, yet its cache eats memory at long contexts. The team varies architectures, sizes, lengths, and data sets to map the trade-offs. Around ten percent of dimensions, they find, matches full RoPE convergence. Partial RoPE also cuts cache memory up to tenfold. NoPE, by contrast, can spike in loss, though a little RoPE or QK-Norm tames the spikes.
arxiv-2603-11711: Zhao and Curtis compare two ways to measure uncertainty in seismic full waveform inversion. The method images Earth's subsurface at high resolution, yet every solution carries uncertainty. One route runs a full nonlinear inversion and reads the whole posterior density. The other linearizes the physics near the best fit and treats the posterior as Gaussian. The team applies both to 2D acoustic problems, with a variational approach for the nonlinear case. Their uncertainty maps differ sharply, most around layer interfaces.
arxiv-2603-12211: Bender and co-authors bound fragmentation in B-trees when insertions arrive in batches. Internal fragmentation is a basic design worry for database structures. Yao's classic result shows even leaf splitting gives good space use under uniform random inserts. Many real workloads instead insert small runs of keys at one spot. The team reworks Yao's analysis to cover such batched workloads in a rigorous way. Even splitting holds up for much of the wider class, and simple fallback strategies cover the rest.
arxiv-2603-12411: Johnson and co-authors distribute quantum workloads across many small processors with adaptive circuit knitting. Single QPUs stay too small for practical advantage, and fast quantum links are lacking. Circuit knitting cuts large circuits into sub-circuits joined by classical communication alone. Plain reconstruction pays exponential sampling costs for that split. Their adaptive method hunts regions of minimal entanglement to place the cuts. Simulations of disordered Ising models up to 60 qubits cut knitting overheads by as much as ten thousand times.
arxiv-2603-12511: Barcomb and co-authors argue that software fairness testing sits inside culture, not above it. Fairness metrics, they note, encode certain cultural values while sidelining others. Test datasets mostly come from Western contexts and miss knowledge held in oral traditions and Indigenous languages. Testing also leans on low-paid labeling work done in the Global South. The energy costs of large models fall hardest on climate-vulnerable populations. The authors call for frameworks that respect many cultures and the right to say no to automated decisions.
arxiv-2603-12911: Hiwa Ahmed and co-authors probe how chiral and axial symmetries restore at high temperature in holographic QCD. Their soft-wall model uses two parameter sets, both tuned to the known crossover temperature and pion mass. Light and strange condensates confirm a smooth chiral crossover in both cases. Chiral partner mesons turn degenerate near that point, a clear sign of restoration. The axial indicator, though, vanishes only at a higher temperature. Axial restoration thus sits on a distinct scale in this frame.
arxiv-2603-13011: Francesco Sinigaglia and co-authors run full simulation-based inference on the Lyman-alpha forest power spectrum for the first time. They use CAMELS simulations with two galaxy formation models, IllustrisTNG and SIMBA. A normalizing flow learns posteriors for two cosmological and four feedback parameters. Within one physics model, cosmology came back close to the true values. Cross-model tests biased one key parameter, which shows model mismatch risk. Training on both models together restored unbiased results.
arxiv-2603-13411: Jiongchi Yu and co-authors review human-in-the-loop approaches for fuzz testing and map the road ahead. Fuzz testing finds bugs well, but automated heuristics often miss deep or complex flaws. Human expert guidance could help, yet no systematic roadmap joins the two fields yet. The authors highlight visualization for interpretable fuzzing and on-the-fly interventions that steer fuzzers to hard program behaviors. LLMs raise fresh questions about how experts share actionable knowledge. Their agenda covers monitoring, steering, and human-LLM collaboration.
arxiv-2603-14111: Liu and co-authors release OasisSimp, a dataset for sentence simplification in five languages: English, Sinhala, Tamil, Pashto, and Thai. For Thai, Pashto, and Tamil, no such dataset existed before. Trained annotators rewrote sentences under strict rules that guard meaning, fluency, and grammar. The team tests eight open multilingual language models on the data. Scores drop sharply for low-resource languages versus English, which exposes how weak current simplification methods remain outside rich-data settings.
arxiv-2603-14311: Wang and co-authors show how quantum synchronization can break down into a boundary time crystal. Sync in driven, lossy systems is often read from smooth phase locking, with no clear test for a true transition. Their Liouvillian frame sorts systems by the attractor of their undriven background. A self-sustained oscillator background supports sturdy time crystals off resonance. A polar fixed point background holds them only at resonance. Sharp dynamic and spectral signs mark the change.
arxiv-2603-14411: Flad and co-authors survey redundancy systems for fault-tolerant design, with a focus on triple modular redundancy. The field suffers from split naming, where the same method hides under many labels. The survey sets one taxonomy across spatial, temporal, and mixed strategies. A new five-class scheme sorts voter designs as well. Findings weigh costly spatial TMR for safety-critical gear against lean temporal methods. Mixed and adaptive TMR gain ground for AI accelerators, and gaps like multi-bit upsets are flagged.
arxiv-2603-14511: Clarkson and Maartens revisit galaxy peculiar velocity growth in general relativity. Some recent work claims the covariant 1+3 approach predicts far stronger growth than standard theory. That claim says standard methods act Newtonian while the covariant one stays fully relativistic. The authors show the claim fails under consistent use. Treated with care, the covariant equations match the standard result exactly. Past strong-growth claims came from terms used as free sources. Such flows cannot mimic cosmic acceleration, they argue.
arxiv-2603-14911: Mosievskiy fine-tunes RoBERTa to map vulnerability descriptions to weakness classes, rivaling far larger models. The training set holds 234,770 CVE texts with AI-refined CWE labels. Agreement-filtered test sets check the model where human and AI labels concur. Top-1 accuracy hits 87.4% across 205 weakness classes. Macro F1 reaches 60.7%, a 15.5-point jump over a TF-IDF baseline. Rare classes drive much of that edge. On CTI-Bench, strict accuracy of 75.6% ties an 8B reasoning model. The small model uses 64 times fewer parameters.
arxiv-2603-15311: Zhang and co-authors work out where the radiative near field ends in millimeter-wave and terahertz links with misaligned antenna arrays. Short wavelengths stretch the near field, so far-field rules fail close in. Most earlier work ignored arrays at both ends or assumed perfect alignment. Their framework handles varied rotations and misalignments for linear and planar arrays. Closed-form formulas give the boundary distance for array-to-array and array-to-point setups. Numerics show misalignment can shift the near-field boundary a lot.
arxiv-2603-15411: Solow and co-authors blend neural networks with biophysical crop models to predict phenology stages and cold hardiness. Pure physics models lack site-level precision, while pure deep learning can break biological sense and needs much data. Their network predicts the parameters of a differentiable biophysical model instead of the crop state itself. Multi-task learning shares data across cultivars. On real and synthetic data, phenology accuracy rose by 60 percent over deployed models. Cold hardiness accuracy rose by 40 percent.
arxiv-2603-15511: Fassino and Uberti give a new way to compute risk budgeting portfolios, where each asset adds a preset share of the total risk. Their route builds a Cauchy sequence inside the simplex of portfolio weights. Its limit is the risk budgeting portfolio. This yields a direct, efficient algorithm with no side optimization problems. The portfolio also appears as a fixed point of a map they define, which supplies existence and uniqueness tests. They develop the method for general risk measures, in detail for standard deviation.
arxiv-2603-15611: Wang and co-authors build Code-A1, a training setup where two language models push against each other. One model writes code and gains reward for passing tests. A second model writes tests and gains reward for finding defects. Keeping the roles apart stops the cheating seen in single-model self-play. The test model can read candidate code and craft targeted attacks. A Mistake Book replays past errors during training. Tests on Qwen2.5-Coder models match or beat training with human-written tests.
arxiv-2603-16011: Sehgal and co-authors benchmark coding agents on real codebase speed work. Synthetic tasks miss the mess of true repository optimization. FormulaCode mines 957 bottlenecks from scientific Python projects. Expert patches pair with each mined bottleneck case. Each task averages 264.6 community performance workloads. Agents face correctness and speed goals at the same time. Fine-grained scores grade many traits past pass or fail. Frontier agents still struggle at this scale, they find. Repository-wide, multi-goal optimization stays an open challenge.
arxiv-2603-16111: Mantovanelli proves a dyadic frequency law for a bent Hofstadter Q sequence. The perturbed recursion adds a signed term to the classic rule. Cloître showed it stays well-defined for all steps. Every value lands odd, so counts group by half-shifted size. F counts how often each odd value appears. Inside each dyadic block, the frequency multiset takes a set form. The form adds 3 to the 2-adic count of each index. Plateau times and gap degrees drive the proof. A central-pair lemma seals the cut.
arxiv-2603-16311: Hegde maps the phase landscape of the doped Mott insulator from a t/U series. Analysis of the series reveals a uniform altermagnet across the region. Kinetic effects drive it. The altermagnet sits between the antiferromagnet and the d-wave superconductor. That slot is normally held by the pseudogap. Its boundary splits the superconductor into underdoped and overdoped parts. The state is unstable to patchy spin and charge order. It tends most strongly toward a pi-flux state.
arxiv-2603-16411: Kumar and Sachdeva fix entity errors in speech recognition output. Rare and domain terms are often mangled or dropped entirely. Their RECOVER agent works after recognition, using tools. It gathers several recognition hypotheses as evidence. Then it retrieves candidate entities and corrects with a language model under constraints. Four hypothesis strategies are compared. Across five datasets, entity error rates fell by 8 to 46 percent. Recall rose by up to 22 points.
arxiv-2603-16811: Bogachev and co-authors study the phase of light waves crossing a turbulent medium. They focus on strong scintillation, where the Rytov variance is large. In that regime, the pair correlation of phase gradients can be tied to a known envelope correlation, if the envelope is assumed Gaussian. Their simulations show the computed profile nears the theory as the variance grows, for distances below the Fried length. At larger distances the match breaks down, because the envelope stops being Gaussian.
arxiv-2603-16911: Benavides-Martinez and co-authors study how AlphaEarth embedding vectors organize land cover information. These geospatial vectors predict well, but their inner structure is obscure. The team asks what each dimension adds, using importance scores and staged removal tests. They find a spectrum of roles. Some dimensions serve one land cover class. Others are shared across classes, and the broadest track wide environmental gradients. Top accuracy held with only 2 to 12 of the 64 dimensions in use. The authors say this spare capacity could cut computing costs.
arxiv-2603-17011: Waisberg and Katz confirm that the star Nunki, also called Sigma Sagittarii, is a close binary and a nearby supernova progenitor candidate. Earlier interferometry had hinted at two stars of roughly six solar masses each. Combining newer and archival observations, the authors solve the orbit: a period of about 135 days and a separation just over one astronomical unit. At about 69 parsecs, Nunki is closer than Spica or Bellatrix. Its eccentric orbit may later force a merger. They also show Bellatrix has no close equal mass companion.
arxiv-2603-17111: Bugaud exposes a family bias hidden inside vision language model ensembles. Ensembles mix models from many providers to raise accuracy, but models from one family share correlated errors. Across 17 models from 8 families, he finds family correlation cuts the effective voter count to about 3. On a small misleading tier of questions, correlated majorities drive accuracy to zero even when the best model is right. He proposes three family aware fixes. The strongest, learned candidate scoring, gains on all three benchmarks and never degrades any of them.
arxiv-2603-18611: Nguyen, Rudra, and Nejdl build a crisis classifier that explains itself across text and images. Social posts during disasters carry news on damage, missing people, and stranded groups. Their method learns a joint text-image representation with a visual language transformer. Text rationales come first, then map onto image regions. Final labels rest on the extracted rationales alone. On CrisisMMD, macro F1 rises by 2 to 35 percent over prior work. Human raters prefer its image patches, and zero-shot accuracy hits 80 percent on new data.
arxiv-2603-18911: Pandya presents a four-stage training plan for chat systems that cite their sources in English and Hindi. Stages cover language tuning, cited English chat, two-language chat, and a final reward step. Six models are tested at each stage. Citation training cuts made-up claims to zero for some model types from stage two on. The staged plan also guards Hindi skill while English grows. Three checks trace how citation habits form across training, not just whether they form.
arxiv-2603-19011: Bottazzi and Park test whether language model agents can tell safe deal rooms from unsafe ones. In such rooms, shared secrets are wiped if no deal is struck, so full sharing is the smart move. Agents must judge safety from clues in their prompt alone. Ten models face varied proof setups in a negotiation task. A failed safety proof cuts sharing in every model. A passed proof gives mixed effects. Some share more, some stay flat, and a few share less, they find.
arxiv-2603-19311: Singhal and co-authors tune prompts by taste rather than by labeled answers. Their PrefPO needs only a start prompt and plain criteria in words. A judge model states which of two outputs it prefers and why. An optimizer model then rewrites the prompt in light of that feedback. On nine hard reasoning tasks, it matches or beats top methods on six. Without any labels, it still matches its labeled scores on six tasks. Its prompts stay far shorter and less repetitive than rivals.
arxiv-2603-19411: Coghi and Garrahan derive a large deviation rule for jump processes that feed back on themselves. In these systems, jump rates depend on what the process has done so far. The rule covers joint swings in occupation share and flow between states. An exponential tilting trick drives the derivation of the full result. A split appears between fast micro dynamics and slow memory drift. The team then proves kinetic and thermodynamic uncertainty bounds for such systems. Simple cases show how the new bounds perform in practice.
arxiv-2603-19611: Tong and co-authors give a theoretical analysis of in-context learning in language models. They link test loss to three factors under mild assumptions. First, the quality of chosen demonstrations, measured along paths to pretraining samples. Second, the model's built-in in-context skill. Third, the degree of distribution shift. Chain-of-thought helps when each substep has good demonstrations and simpler subtasks. Template sensitivity also changes with the number of demonstrations. Experiments back the theory throughout.
arxiv-2603-20011: Jeon, Wong, and Chae build an analytic frame for fluid antenna systems paired with active reflecting surfaces. The pairing suits 6G links that need flexible control of the radio environment. Fluid antennas can switch ports, while the active surface amplifies the signal. The authors first find the best gain under a power limit. They then derive a tractable outage formula and a tight upper bound. A monotone link between outage and channel gain yields closed form phase tuning. A region based throughput method reaches near optimal rates.
arxiv-2603-20111: Gögl and Yau recast the joint embedding predictive architecture as a variational method. JEPA models predict in representation space rather than rebuild raw inputs. The authors argue JEPA's split from generative modelling is more rhetoric than structure. Its coupled encoders mirror variational posteriors and learned conditional priors. Standard JEPA then looks like a deterministic special case with heuristic safeguards. Their Var-JEPA makes the latent generative structure explicit. It optimizes a single evidence lower bound, with no ad hoc anti collapse tricks. A tabular version learned strong representations.
arxiv-2603-20211: Riahi and co-authors study how middle school teachers interact with chatbots during a coding activity. Eleven teacher teams used chatbots inside a block-based programming setting for science. Audio transcripts and chat logs feed a qualitative analysis. Three teacher profiles emerge: explorer, frustrated, and mixed, each needing different support. Teachers praised gains in prompting skill and confidence. They also feared losses in learning and critical thinking for students. Design advice covers staged chatbot introductions and teacher control of features. Guidance on when to use chatbots rounds out the findings.
arxiv-2603-20311: Siva and co-authors introduce kRAIG, an agent that builds data pipelines from plain language requests. Hand-building extract, transform, and load workflows is slow and needs deep expertise. kRAIG writes production-ready Kubeflow pipelines end to end. Its ReQuesAct method asks clarifying questions before building, fixing vague intent. It also checks pipeline integrity with language model validation before execution. The system tripled extraction and loading success versus agentic baselines. Transformation accuracy rose by 25 percent as well.
arxiv-2603-20511: Zhong and co-authors present CARE, a framework to judge health AI tools by what users can truly do. Standard tests score task success and chat quality at the system level. CARE adds capability outcomes drawn from the capability approach. One lens lists the resources and capabilities a system should support. A second lens checks how design and social context shape those outcomes. They apply CARE to reproductive health chatbots, general LLMs, and search tools. In a study with twelve users, the same features helped some and held back others.
arxiv-2603-20711: Zheng and co-authors present RoboECC, a way to split vision language action models between edge and cloud. These robot models cost a lot to run in real time. A poor split point can waste the edge device or the link. Their method picks split points with both model shape and hardware in mind. It then adjusts the split as network bandwidth shifts. Tests across models gave speedups up to 3.28 times. Extra cost stayed near 2.6 percent in their trials.
arxiv-2603-20911: Peng and co-authors test whether language model agents show real engagement patterns in a social media simulation. Fluent, human-like output alone does not prove a theory, they note. In a Weibo-like setting, they vary information load and descriptive norms. Popularity cues, such as likes and reshares, grow inside the simulation itself. Agent engagement responds in clear ways to load and norms. Sensitivity to popularity cues changes with context, rather than staying fixed. They draw lessons for simulation based communication research, including stress tests and clear baseline design.
arxiv-2603-21111: Liu and co-authors present Free Sinewich, a parameter-efficient method for multi-task fine tuning. Most efficient fine tuning methods adapt a model to one task at a time. Their layer mixes low-rank factors and convolutional priors into one kernel. A sinusoidal transform then modulates the kernel to make task specific weights at near zero cost. A small Clock Net produces bounded frequencies that keep the modulation stable. On dense prediction benchmarks, the method beats single task fine tuning while using few trainable parameters.
arxiv-2603-21311: Monika and co-authors study how the numerical index of a Banach space behaves under subspace convergence. The numerical index is a geometric constant that relates an operator's numerical radius to its norm. In the operator opening topology, they prove a full limit theorem: the index of converging subspaces tends to the index of the limit space. With ultraproduct methods, they show the numerical radius is preserved exactly by ultraproduct operators. As a result, every ultrapower has numerical index no larger than the original space.
arxiv-2603-21411: Yang and co-authors work on fingerprinting neural networks so owners can prove a model is theirs. Fingerprints built from adversarial examples work, but nobody knew how far from the decision boundary they should sit. Their AnaFP scheme sets that distance with a tunable stretch factor. They derive bounds that the factor must respect for robustness and uniqueness. Grid search then picks a workable value. In tests, AnaFP beat prior methods across architectures and modification attacks.
arxiv-2603-21611: Jia and co-authors present SARe, a generative system that reassembles broken 3D objects from unordered fragments. As fragment counts grow, weak shape cues and exploding contact options make the puzzle hard. SARe conditions its flow-based assembly on local geometry around each surface query. Extra supervision heads teach fracture regions and fragment contacts while the flow trains, shaping the features that move points. A refinement pass verifies predicted relations and resamples only the doubtful fragments. Tests on synthetic and real fractured objects reached state-of-the-art part accuracy.
arxiv-2603-21711: Lentjes and de Wolff define a new tool, the characteristic operator, for a class of linear operators. They study how its spectrum behaves. The work aims at periodic evolution equations. They give a step-by-step scheme to build the tool for many cases. Examples cover classic delay equations, delay equations with infinite delay, and mixed functional equations. For that last class, they settle an open problem on Floquet exponents and their discrete structure. The results extend work by Kaashoek and Verduyn Lunel on characteristic matrices.
arxiv-2603-21811: Hageman reformulates cohesive phase-field fracture so it runs like a standard material model in finite element codes. Classic phase-field methods grow cracks from fracture energy alone and cannot set a material strength for crack birth. Eigenstrain versions fix that, but they relied on global energy minimization setups. Hageman exploits the fact that fracture eigenstrains need no spatial gradients. Crack growth then becomes a local update at each integration point, like plasticity. Tests on holed and notched plates gave mesh-independent results and captured crack branching under dynamic loads.
arxiv-2603-21911: Ben Azizi and co-authors emulate spectral images with a variational model that reports uncertainty. Physics-based transfer models can fake such images, but run slowly. Learned emulators are fast, yet most give one fixed answer with no sense of doubt. Their framework treats emulation as a latent-variable problem, with two-step pretraining and latent mapping. Tests cover simulated vegetation cubes (211 bands) and real ocean-color images (21 bands). No design won everywhere: pixel models led on clean simulations, while a spatial model held up better on noisy real data.
arxiv-2603-22011: Ding and co-authors build two secret sharing schemes where members hold different levels of authority. In plain secret sharing, every member has equal power. Their schemes split members into ranked groups instead. Both schemes rest on the Chinese remainder theorem for integer rings and on one-way functions. One scheme is disjunctive and the other is conjunctive. The authors prove both schemes are secure. They also show both are asymptotically ideal, a step past older CRT schemes. Older schemes had security flaws or low information rates.
arxiv-2603-22111: Vilvanathan and co-authors use shot noise to study graphene quantum point contacts. Conductance alone cannot show how transmission splits among modes. The team pairs tight-binding simulations with random matrix theory. They test the predictions against conductance maps of graphene Hall bars. Three regimes appear: smooth propagation, sharp mode filtering, and multi-mode mixing. For higher Landau levels, full mixing gives a Fano factor near 1/4. The zeroth Landau level instead settles at 1/3. That split gives a noise signature that separates single-channel from multi-channel transport.
arxiv-2603-22311: Fan and co-authors borrow astronomy tools to spot tiny calcium signals in brain cells. Fluorescence imaging tracks synaptic calcium transients in real time. These signals sit barely above background, so software often misses them. Astronomy faces the same hunt for faint transients over wide fields. Their algorithm, Astro-BEATS, adapts background estimation and source finding from that field. It beats threshold-based methods at detection and segmentation. Its masks can train deep learning models for harder data. It also runs on new datasets with no re-tuning.
arxiv-2603-22411: Kim and co-authors set new limits on dark matter hits on protons in the COSINE-100 detector. The team lowers the event threshold to just three or four photoelectrons. A neural picker and noise control make the low range usable. They search that range for the yearly modulation a dark matter halo should cause. No clear modulation shows up in the data. The limits are the world's tightest for dark matter near two GeV in mass. With the Migdal effect, the reach extends below one GeV.
arxiv-2603-22511: Jimeno and Izal present CTF as a Service, a platform that hosts capture-the-flag security contests for teaching. Running such events takes heavy infrastructure work, which keeps many schools from adopting them. Their system builds on Proxmox virtual machines, Terraform and Ansible automation, Docker Swarm, and an HAProxy load balancer. Challenges deploy straight from a Git repository through a delivery pipeline. The authors report design choices, snags, and fixes covering session persistence, routing, and repeatable setups.
arxiv-2603-22711: Zhang and Wu compute holographic one-point functions for Wilson surfaces. Their case study uses a toroidal surface operator. Compared with flat or spherical cases, the results depend in richer ways on shape and position. Averaging over the moduli space of dual membranes plays a key role. The authors obtain both analytic and numeric results. They also study a cylindrical surface operator as a second case.
arxiv-2603-23011: Di Bello and co-authors compare local and global master equations through non-Hermitian physics. Their test case is a two-qubit setup carrying a heat current. Non-Hermitian models can extend phase diagrams, but often rely on postselection. Exceptional points appear only in the local master equation and its non-Hermitian twin, they find. That holds at strong nonequilibrium. Hybrid setups mix Lindblad and non-Hermitian baths. The work clarifies how quantum jumps and exceptional points shape open-system behavior.
arxiv-2603-23111: Mallon and Wang build a global form of Koszul duality. One side holds dg cocommutative coalgebras, which need not be conilpotent here. The other side holds curved Lie algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. They give a model structure for the first class and an infinity-category structure for the second. Two classic functors, Harrison and Chevalley-Eilenberg, are then extended to these wider classes. The pair forms an equivalence of infinity-categories, they show.
arxiv-2603-23411: Lin and Heng apply deformation quantization to systems with second-class constraints. Such systems call for the Dirac bracket rather than the Poisson bracket. The pair pick a star product whose first quantum term tracks the Dirac bracket. They test the scheme on an oscillator in a deformed fermionic phase space. They compute its energy levels and Wigner functions under that scheme. They also study the entanglement entropy that the phase space deformation induces.
arxiv-2603-23611: Cho, Ruberto, and Terragni present LLMORPH, a tool that tests language models without human-labeled answers. Checking model output lacks a cheap oracle, which blocks routine testing. Metamorphic testing sidesteps the oracle by mutating inputs and watching for broken relations. LLMORPH wraps that idea for language tasks and any model or relation set. The team ran 36 relations on four benchmarks against three top models. That produced over 561,000 test executions. The tool reliably exposes inconsistencies in model behavior.
arxiv-2603-23811: Kwon and co-authors present a speculative video work about career advice and trust in AI. Participants thought they were chatting with a career counseling AI agent. The replies in fact came from a mudang, a Korean traditional shaman, doing fortune-telling. After the reveal, participants kept their first views of the advice. They did not downgrade it once they knew the source. The piece uses this trick to ask how much explainability and accuracy matter, and to probe human agency in the AI age.
arxiv-2603-23911: Zhao and co-authors present MTP-D, a self-distillation method that speeds up language model inference. Multi-token prediction lets a model guess several future tokens at once, but extra heads are often rejected. MTP-D distills knowledge within the same model at little extra training cost. It raises head acceptance by 7.5 percent while keeping main-head quality. A looped extension adds more heads cheaply and speeds inference by 220.4 percent over one-head prediction. Tests span seven benchmarks.
arxiv-2603-24011: Chen and Xie study baryon-antibaryon pairs made in electron-positron collisions. They track spin and entanglement through cascade decays. They derive a full spin density matrix in terms of measured spin quantities. Compact recursive rules extend the method to multi-step cascades. When a decay breaks parity to the max, the final particles are fully polarized and not entangled. With CP conserved, paired charge-conjugate decays can amplify entanglement when the first pair is polarized, they show.
arxiv-2603-24311: Ghosh uses a quantum annealer to map phase boundaries in frustrated Ising magnets. The model family covers materials such as MNb2O6 and BaCo2V2O8. Competing couplings create a sign problem that blocks quantum Monte Carlo at any size. On a D-Wave Advantage2 machine with up to 729 spins, Ghosh measures quantum-driven transitions at four anisotropy values. Quasi-one-dimensional cases share a suppression ratio near 0.450, so quantum effects erase about 55 percent of the classical stability window. Two blind predictions confirmed the crossover law in advance.
arxiv-2603-24511: Panfilov and co-authors show that AI agents in an autoresearch loop can discover state-of-the-art attack algorithms against language models. Frontier agents such as Claude Code and Codex worked with a library of over 30 prior methods and a fixed compute budget. Against a safeguard model, the best agent-found method reached up to 80 percent attack success on CBRNE queries, versus under 50 percent for known methods. Against an adversarially trained model, success hit 100 percent. The authors also trace how the methods evolved during the search.
arxiv-2603-25011: Nguyen and co-authors speed up learned sparse retrieval with a fused GPU kernel called Sparton. Sparse retrieval models project hidden states into a word-sized matrix, then shrink it to a sparse form. Writing that full matrix wastes memory and slows training. Sparton merges the matrix product, activation steps, and max reduction into one Triton kernel. It reduces tiles on the fly, so the big matrix never exists. Alone it runs up to 4.8 times faster with far less peak memory. Inside Splade, batch size grows by a third.
arxiv-2603-25111: Banerjee and co-authors add proof to self-improving AI agents with SEVerA. Such agents write their own code and tune it per task, but nothing checks their safety. The team frames agent building as learning under hard rules. Each model call gets a formal output contract in first-order logic. A rejection sampler with a checked fallback guards each call. Search, proof, and learning stages then tune the agent without breaking the rules. Across proof, math, and tool tasks, violations stay at zero while scores beat prior systems.
arxiv-2603-25511: Deng, Wang, and Zhou prove a Brezis-Merle style bound for the k-Hessian equation. The bound governs k-convex functions that vanish at the border of their domain. As a payoff, they get an Alexandrov-Bakelman-Pucci estimate for the mid-level Hessian equation. That kind of estimate caps a solution by the size of its source term. They also build a concentration-compactness rule for how solutions of the mean-field k-Hessian equation can blow up. The tools serve a hard class of fully nonlinear equations.
arxiv-2603-25811: Hernandez-Sanchez and co-authors propose a method for reaching value agreements in a diverse society. People may share core values yet weigh them differently and read them in different ways. Most past work seeks a single agreement for all. Their method lets agents state their value systems and how much they will concede. A decentralized search then finds a set of agreements that fit the spread. Tests use data from a value evaluation study and the European Value Survey. The authors report clear gains over older methods.
arxiv-2603-25911: Hirari and co-authors build a regression method for tensor data that resists outliers. Tensor-on-tensor regression predicts response tensors from predictor tensors. Standard fits break when outliers strike whole cases or single cells. Their method, ROTOT, handles both kinds at once and copes with missing values. One loss function limits the pull of bad cells in the response. A robust component analysis cleans the predictors. New plots help users see which outliers were found. Tests include simulations and a face dataset used to predict facial traits.
arxiv-2603-26111: Smolec and co-authors extend a grid of Cepheid star models built with the MESA code. This third part adds core and envelope overshooting to the models. Tracks cover stars of two to eight solar masses and a wide metal range. Pulsation traits come from a matched MESA module. The team gives instability strip edges, ages, and period change rates. Relations link period to luminosity, radius, and age. The metal effect matches recent observations well. Short-period Cepheids in the Small Magellanic Cloud remain hard to reproduce.
arxiv-2603-26211: Kumbhar and co-authors test whether discrete diffusion vision-language models can locate elements on a screen. They adapt the LLaDA-V model to predict actions and bounding boxes for web, desktop, and mobile screens. A hybrid masking schedule that mixes linear and fixed masking lifts step success by up to 6.1 points. More training data from varied GUI domains cuts delay by about 1.3 seconds. Accuracy also rises by an average of 20 points across tests.
arxiv-2603-26311: Busse and Toikka present the Majorana-XYZ subsystem code for quantum error correction. One form stores one logical qubit in an L by L grid of physical qubits, with distance L. A second form stores nearly n logical qubits at distance 3 as a standard stabiliser code. Single-qubit gates act transversally in the subsystem form. Under X and Z noise, the team finds thresholds near 1.4% for odd distance and 1.8% for even distance.
arxiv-2603-26511: Simplício and co-authors introduce AMALIA, a fully open language model built for European Portuguese. That variant is scarce in training data, and translated tests can miss its local traits. AMALIA uses more high-quality European Portuguese text in both mid-training and post-training stages. The team also releases native benchmarks, with translated tasks plus four new sets on generation, language skill, and bias between variants. AMALIA matches strong rivals on translated tests and clearly beats them on native ones.
arxiv-2603-26611: Izbicki and Rodrigues benchmark tabular foundation models as tools for conditional density estimation. The task asks for the full spread of a response given table inputs, not just one point guess. Models like TabPFN and TabICL output predictive distributions by nature, yet their density skill was untested. The team scores three variants against parametric, tree, and neural rivals on 39 datasets. Foundation models win on density loss, log-likelihood, and CRPS for most sets and sizes. A galaxy redshift case shows TabPFN beating rivals trained on ten times more data.
arxiv-2603-27011: Safdari Fesaghandis and Maity introduce ParsCN, the first Persian dataset for counter-narrative generation. Such replies answer hate speech with constructive responses instead of censorship. ParsCN holds 1,100 hate speech and reply pairs. Labels cover six target groups and six countering strategies, tuned to Persian online culture. A multi-stage pipeline mixes human annotation with model-augmented generation and hand curation. Human-written replies scored highest on relevance, fluency, and tone. Benchmark models still struggled with fluency, cultural nuance, and safety.
arxiv-2603-27311: Vakondios and Anastopoulos study time of arrival for relativistic particles moving on a ring, within quantum field theory. On a ring, a particle may pass the detector several times first. That makes the interaction itself part of the theory's job. Their quantum temporal probabilities method derives detection measures from the field theory. Detection chances are checked in semiclassical and fully quantum regimes. For particle ensembles, the signal repeats in a cycle like a quantum clock. Rotating rings add noise that mirrors the rotational Unruh effect.
arxiv-2603-27511: Ghanavat and co-authors move quantum entanglement along a two-leg spin ladder. A selective field acts only on the rungs in between. The run starts with a fully entangled rung pair. That state reaches the far pair with fidelity 0.9998. Middle rungs stay near disentangled throughout. Two timescales shape the motion. A fast local swing sets one scale. A slow envelope driven by field strength sets the other. The transfer stays robust under ten percent disorder.
arxiv-2603-27911: Petrov and co-authors raise photocurrent readout contrast in diamond NV centers. PDMR reads magnetic resonance through photoelectric signals. Contrast reaches fifty percent and above in single centers. The team locates features that generate the photocurrent. Electrons from the center rest in interface trap levels. Those states act as an amplifier stage. A second laser can drive that amplifier. A model explains the gains without bias voltage.
arxiv-2603-28111: Matsumoto asks when a dg-category counts as a phantom, meaning its additive invariants all vanish. He works with admissible subcategories of the derived category of a smooth proper variety. He builds a non-compact motive for such a category and shows its realizations recover its K-theory, topological K-theory, and cyclic homology. If the variety's Chow motive is finite, vanishing of any of these invariants forces the category's rational motive to vanish. He also proves phantomness persists in smooth families.
arxiv-2603-28511: Beunen and five co-authors study how gas bubbles clog and clear narrow throats in porous layers, a key flow inside water electrolyzers. They mix theory, 3D lattice Boltzmann simulations, and X-ray imaging of single bubbles, pairs, and chains. For one bubble they derive the Bond number that splits passage from clogging. Pairs open new routes: pressure in the film between bubbles can blast a clog free, while merging can jam or free the pair. Foam tests confirm the map.
arxiv-2603-29211: Zhang and co-authors present Xuanwu VL-2B, a multimodal model built for content ecosystems. General models often lose accuracy on moderation and adversarial content. The model pairs a compact vision encoder with a 1.7-billion-parameter language model. Training runs in three stages, from pretraining to post-training. A data curation loop balances business skill with general ability. The model scored 67.90 on average across seven OpenCompass metrics. It reached 94.38 percent recall across seven moderation tasks.
arxiv-2603-29511: Pruzhinskaya and co-authors report the first year of anomaly hunting in the Fink broker. Wide surveys send alert streams where rare events hide. Their pipeline turns Zwicky Transient Facility light curves into compact features. An Isolation Forest ranks alerts, trained on archival data. Each night, the ten oddest cases go to experts for review. A feedback loop retrains the model from expert votes. The year brought finds like a rare AM CVn system and nine new dwarf novae. It also triggered 33 supernovae, most of them new.
arxiv-2603-29611: Schaefer and Drossel compare the modes of two matrices on random geometric graphs in 2D. The matrices are the graph Laplacian and the adjacency matrix. They diagonalize both across many sizes and link counts. For the adjacency matrix, all modes localize once systems get large. The Laplacian always keeps a few modes that span the whole system. A conservation law explains that split. It also shapes the spread of participation ratios. They sort out the roles of size, degree, and motifs.
arxiv-2603-29811: Copatti and co-authors build new quantum Floquet codes on compact surfaces. They cover both orientable and non-orientable cases. Their route views surfaces as hyperbolic polygons with semi-regular tilings. This extends earlier Floquet code work on surfaces of genus at least two. They also study how the codes perform. An analysis of long-run behavior rounds out the results.
arxiv-2604-00311: Waegell sets out what nonsuperdeterminism demands of a theory, setting a standard for ruling a theory nonsuperdeterministic. Superdeterminism now means theories producing steady breaks of statistical independence, offered as a local causal account of Bell links. He examines how ontic states and response functions fix outcomes, and how vetted sampling differs across the two kinds of theory. The result: individual samples and outcomes must mirror observed distributions, a standard that defines freedom and independence. He shows superdeterminism is usually contextual, and theories can yield the same data.
arxiv-2604-00411: Ke and colleagues propose a ring-based scheme for private information retrieval with error detection. The best current method leans on distributed point functions, but its finite-field design forces prime-order functions with very large keys under information-theoretic privacy. Its dual-key layout also adds needless traffic. Built over a prime-power ring instead, the new scheme sidesteps the field constraint, uses its point functions more efficiently, and shrinks keys sharply for large deployments.
arxiv-2604-00911: Antonin Sulc tests whether strict building-block structure in sequence vectors yields real spatial organization in protein networks. With Event2Vec, a model that adds vectors, he trains vectors with 64 numbers on walks taken at random from the human STRING interactome and sets them against a DeepWalk standard. That structure sharply lifts pathway coherence, analogy accuracy, and layered pathway organization, while some spatial traits match or trail the standard.
arxiv-2604-01111: Ladra and Pérez-Rodríguez take on modularity for evolution algebras, a trait looked at before but still not fully mapped in many natural cases. They map modular evolution algebras fully for the nilpotent case, where products end at zero. They also cover supersolvable regular evolution algebras, where a chain of ideals gives the algebra its shape.
arxiv-2604-01211: Khanpour, Turizo, and Talkington study how to split a limited bit budget across sensor readings that use different quantizations. They judge designs by the trace of the error covariance of a linear minimum mean square error state estimator, an A-optimal criterion. A formula reduces each gradient evaluation to one Cholesky factorization, enabling a Frank-Wolfe method and a second solver based on interior points with an L-BFGS Hessian guess. Tests on IEEE power grid cases up to 300 buses show the analytic gradient is the key enabler.
arxiv-2604-01311: Zouhair, El Guermai and Ouelddris study impulse control of degenerate singular parabolic equations. In such systems diffusion can vanish or blow up at points. Their goal is steering solutions to rest in finite time. They give an explicit estimate for how fast solutions decay exponentially, proving it by combining a logarithmic convexity estimate with special spectral properties. They also establish that a minimal-norm impulse control exists and is unique, giving the cheapest possible intervention, in norm, that achieves the stabilization.
arxiv-2604-01411: Roberts and colleagues present Train-to-Test scaling laws optimizing model size, training tokens and inference sample count under end-to-end budgets. Modern language models scale at test time through repeated sampling, a trade-off Chinchilla style pretraining scaling laws do not address. Across eight downstream tasks, accounting for inference cost shifts optimal pretraining decisions into the overtraining regime, well outside scaling suites. They validate the forecasts by pretraining overtrained models in the forecast optimal region, confirming stronger performance than pretraining scaling alone. The findings survive post-training.
arxiv-2604-01811: Kreis and colleagues present GPU-RMQ for range minimum queries on GPUs, used in string and database work. Recent ray-tracing approaches express queries as rays fired into triangles for range minima, but suffer memory overhead, slow building, or low throughput. GPU-RMQ builds a hierarchy of summaries in parallel, then processes parts in a parallel scan. Its hybrid design uses ray tracing cores and CUDA cores at different levels. Tests show higher throughput than leading GPU methods, on large arrays, with a smaller footprint and faster index construction.
arxiv-2604-02211: Ranganathan and colleagues survey multi agent video recommenders, systems that shape what billions watch. Single model recommenders that chase static engagement scores struggle with modern platform demands. Agent teams that split video understanding, reasoning, memory and feedback now serve, learn and adapt together. The survey traces their rise from early reinforcement learning systems to language model powered designs, maps collaboration patterns, and flags open problems in scale, multimodal understanding and incentive alignment.
arxiv-2604-02411: Csáki and colleagues build the QCD axion holographically from a warped five dimensional model. A bulk scalar field, dual to the topological operator of QCD, makes relations among the axion and the anomalies transparent. Bulk modes for axion states are identified, with the usual four dimensional axion adjustment. The framework locates the axion quality problem origin, and a large degree of axion compositeness proves necessary to solve it. In the high quality limit, the physical axion lives mostly in the bulk gauge field.
arxiv-2604-02711: Bian and nine colleagues survey foundation models for sensor-based human activity recognition, the task of reading what a person is doing from wearable sensors. Current models struggle with scarce labels, varied sensors, and weak transfer across users and devices. The survey sorts work by a lifecycle taxonomy, tracks nine design axes, and names three development paths, from models trained from scratch on sensor data to adapted general time-series models.
arxiv-2604-02811: Fu and eight colleagues present ChatSVA, an end-to-end system for generating SystemVerilog assertions for hardware verification with task-specific language models. Manual assertion writing is slow and error-prone, while direct model use suffers low accuracy and scarce domain data. Their AgentBridge platform generates high-purity datasets for a multi-agent system, reaching 98.66 percent syntax and 96.12 percent functional pass rates across 24 RTL designs.
arxiv-2604-02911: Liang and seven colleagues present DreamTIP, a framework that improves sim-to-real transfer for quadruped robot locomotion across varied terrain. Traditional transfer leans on hand-designed features or costly real-world tuning. Guided by large language models, DreamTIP identifies task-invariant properties such as contact stability and terrain clearance. It trains them as auxiliary targets inside the Dreamer world model, yielding representations robust to dynamic change.
arxiv-2604-03511: Bothmann and colleagues apply Continuous Normalizing Flows trained with Flow Matching to phase-space draws in Monte Carlo event making for collider work. Covering lepton-pair and top quark pair making with multiple jets, they train helicity-tuned flows that remap random numbers used in matrix element scores. Unweighting rates rise by factors up to 184 and 25 for the two processes at highest jet number. Combined with Coupling Layer flows, time gains reach about tenfold.
arxiv-2604-03611: Sha and colleagues introduce PortraitCraft, a single benchmark for portrait framing reading and making built on about 50,000 picked real portrait images. The dataset carries structured multi-level labels. These include global framing scores, notes over 13 framing traits, trait-level why-texts, image Q&A pairs, and framing-based written blurbs. Two benchmark tasks cover framing reading through score guessing, trait thinking, and image Q&A. The second covers framing-aware making from structured blurbs under explicit rules.
arxiv-2604-03811: Marcelo Cavalcanti and team built a nonlinear analogue of a sharp linear semigroup decay test. The Borichev-Tomilov test reads decay off resolvent growth, a route with no nonlinear spectral theory. The team instead tracked a real resolvent equation as its parameter tends to zero, reading the blow-up rate as the nonlinear scaling. That rate fixes polynomial decay for such systems, recovering the optimal rate for a damped wave equation.
arxiv-2604-03911: Aniketh Iyengar and team built molecular dynamics paths by splitting a hard task into two easy ones. A diffusion model first learned structure generation from a large conformer set, then an interpolator trained on path data kept the steps in line over time. The split taps ample structure data to offset scarce path data. Tests on QM9 and DRUGS sets, plus short protein chains, showed paths with strong geometric, dynamical, and energetic marks.
arxiv-2604-04311: Bergach frames the fastest Fourier transform code as a shortest-path problem on a directed acyclic graph. Many valid layouts exist for one transform, differing in radix, stage order and register blocking, with the same math result but different instruction costs. A context-free model scores stages by measured costs alone, while a context-aware model also records the prior edge type, capturing cache effects like warming. On Apple M1 NEON, context-aware search reaches about 30 GFLOPS against about 22, finding a mixed radix layout no context-free search can find.
arxiv-2604-04411: Kawasaki, Tanaka and Nishida probe how visual document understanding is stored inside vision-language models. Visual document understanding demands sight, text recognition and reasoning over layouts. Yet models are usually judged only on generated replies, which may hide whether required information was truly held. Using linear probing across layers, the authors find a clear gap between inner states and generated replies. Required information often encodes more plainly from middle layers than from the final layer. Fine-tuning middle layers improves probing and reply accuracy while closing the gap.
arxiv-2604-04611: Nakamura tackles free-riders in cross-silo federated learning, where some clients submit fake parameters without training. Chen and colleagues detect free-riders from weight evolving frequency patterns. It struggles against dynamic free-riders who act honestly early and switch later. Nakamura proposes S2-WEF, which simulates mimicking attack patterns on the server side using past global models. It flags clients whose submitted patterns resemble the simulated ones. Experiments across four datasets and five attack types show robust dynamic detection.
arxiv-2604-04711: Katayama, Mauroy and Susuki study Koopman operators for nonlinear systems that take inputs as set parameters. They track how the operator's eigenfunctions shift as the parameter shifts, for a system with a globally stable rest point. Their main result turns the nonlinear system into a finite linear system, with the change of form shifting smoothly with the parameter. For control-affine systems they also give a test for when the shift to bilinear form does not hinge on the parameter at all.
arxiv-2604-05011: AL-Makhlafi and co-authors introduce YMIR, a dataset and model for Yemeni music genre sorting, a tradition underrepresented in Western-focused work. The dataset holds 1,475 chosen audio clips across five Yemeni genres: Sanaani, Hadhrami, Lahji, Tihami, and Adeni. Five Yemeni music experts labeled the clips under a clear protocol, reaching strong agreement with a Fleiss kappa of 0.85. Their classification model, a convolutional neural network, sorts genres from time-frequency features.
arxiv-2604-05811: Zheng and Mei certify second-order optimality from discrete collocation outputs for Bolza control problems. Rebuilding state, control, and costate paths, they bound the second variation by discrete curvature minus rest terms. A positive bound proves sufficiency and informs growth and trust-region sizing, with mesh refinement support. The test runs straight from solver output.
arxiv-2604-06111: Wang Yang and nine colleagues build AgentCE-Bench, a testbed for AI agents that cuts the heavy setup cost of older benchmarks. Agents fill hidden slots in a partly finished schedule under local and global constraints, while two knobs control the task: hidden-slot count sets the horizon and a decoy budget sets difficulty. All tool calls resolve through static JSON files, so evaluation runs fast and reproduces cleanly. Tests across 13 models in 6 domains show wide performance gaps and confirm the benchmark separates models well.
arxiv-2604-06311: Ryczanowski and three colleagues search archives for gamma-ray bursts lensed by galaxy clusters, expected once per thousand bursts yet never confirmed. They cross-match localized Swift bursts with an all-sky cluster sample, finding 17 near a cluster. Fourteen candidates sit above their cluster redshift or fit a higher-redshift origin via the Amati relation, indicating lensing. Magnifications stay below 10 except GRB 071031, possibly above 10 but uncertain. For GRB 050509B, previously assumed at redshift 0.225, their lens model favors redshift above 1 and magnification 2 to 6.
arxiv-2604-06711: Zhang and seven colleagues close the gap in reading oracle bone script. Treating each rare character as a closed-set image label fails, since characters combine a small set of recurring picture parts with meanings that carry across characters. Their agent-led setup grounds parts by sight, then chains part spotting, graph-based fact lookup, and link inference into sound readings. A new expert-checked set, OB-Radix, supplies 1,022 character images and 1,853 component images, and tests on three benchmarks show fuller, sharper readings than baselines.
arxiv-2604-06811: Feng and eight colleagues expose a backdoor threat in skill-based agent systems. Such systems compose reusable skills for modularity and scale, opening an unexamined attack surface. SkillTrojan hides malicious logic inside plausible skills, splits an encrypted payload across benign-looking skill calls, and fires only on a set trigger. It can also auto-build backdoored skills from templates, spreading across agent ecosystems. A set of over 3,000 backdoored skills supports evaluation, and on EHR SQL the attack reaches over 97 percent success while keeping over 89 percent clean accuracy on GPT-5.
arxiv-2604-07011: Baum and seven colleagues ask how the replies of a large language model shift as its tuning knobs change, and how those shifts can be drawn on a map. They treat each knob setting as giving a spread of possible replies, then build a joint flat mirror that places like spreads near each other. The paper proves this map can be guessed from reply samples, and that an unknown knob value can be read back from fresh replies. In trials, distinct knob changes pointed in distinct map directions.
arxiv-2604-07111: Zhou, Rois, and Kagias present a full design loop that shapes the photon density of states in three dimensional photonic metamaterials. That density governs how light and matter trade energy, and it matters for sun power and light driven chemistry. Yet shape and light response link in a tangled, non unique way. The team first trains a forward stand in model that guesses light spectra from mask settings, then runs a generative net backwards to propose masks for a wanted spectrum.
arxiv-2604-07911: Patel tackles context pollution in multi-agent language-model orchestration, where concurrent agents contaminate each other's steering with task state, partial outputs, and pending questions. His Dynamic Attentional Context Scoping lets the orchestrator work in two asymmetric modes. Registry mode holds only short status summaries of at most 200 tokens per agent, staying responsive to everyone. When an agent sends a steering request, Focus mode loads that agent's full context while compressing the rest to registry entries. Isolation is agent-triggered, asymmetric, and deterministic.
arxiv-2604-08011: Yu and four colleagues argue that dense connectivity wastes power in recommenders fed by sparse, high-dimensional inputs. Scaling dense nets like deep MLPs often yields diminishing returns or outright degradation. Their study of industrial click-through-rate models reveals implicit connection sparsity: most learned weights drift toward zero while a small fraction stays prominent. The dense design itself becomes the bottleneck, forcing the model to process vast low-utility links instead of valid signals. SSR prunes connections deliberately so pattern modeling focuses on signals that matter.
arxiv-2604-08411: P. Nieciecki, Plocharski, and Musialski build apartment layouts that follow comfort and use rules instead of copying the flaws baked into real training data. They turn set room placement and closeness standards into trainable loss functions inside a transformer generator, steering it toward livable plans during training. Compared with rivals, their layouts score higher on comfort rules while keeping plans sound and buildable.
arxiv-2604-08611: Trivedi argues that chance in quantum theory turns quasilocal in curved spacetime, much as energy does in general relativity. Reading Hermiticity as inner product conservation, he shows gravity boundaries and horizons turn global probability conservation into a flux balancing rule. Nearby observers then see seeming non Hermiticity while global unitarity holds, with checks in Schwarzschild, Kerr, and FLRW settings and imprints in black hole ringdowns.
arxiv-2604-08711: Ahire and three colleagues track ligament breakup in liquid sheets with a two stage deep learning method that handles one to many splits. A Faster R-CNN detector finds ligaments and droplets in high speed shadow images of a Carbopol gel jet, aided by shape preserving synthetic data, reaching F1 up to 0.872. A transformer augmented classifier then labels frame links as continuation, split, or non link with perfect recall for split events, mapping full split trees.
arxiv-2604-09011: Kessler and seven colleagues review a decade of progress in global models of planetary system formation, using the Bern Model as their example. That framework, developed since before the PlanetS research network began, now includes wind-driven disk evolution, planetesimal evolution, and other advances in planet formation theory. The review also names the model's limits: early dust-to-planetesimal phases, hybrid pebble-planetesimal accretion, simplified interior models, simplified parametrizations, and computational constraints. Some limits were eased during PlanetS, but the authors stress what the model still cannot capture.
